result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks and an all-way stop control, which provides a baseline level of safety. Pedestrians benefit from continuous sidewalks and a bike lane that acts as a buffer from motor vehicle traffic on one side of the street.

hazards.name: Wide Corner Radii
hazards.description: The corners of the intersection appear wide, which can encourage vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection where the crosswalks meet the curbs.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes (including a bike lane and parking lane) without a median or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked zebra crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalks
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalks to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting fixtures at a lower height specifically directed at the sidewalks and crosswalks to improve nighttime safety.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous concrete sidewalk that is interrupted by a very wide driveway for an industrial tire shop. The area lacks any pedestrian-scale amenities, buffers from the roadway, or marked crossing infrastructure, creating a hostile environment for walking.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: The tire shop has an exceptionally wide curb cut that forces pedestrians to cross a large area where vehicles may enter or exit at various angles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center right, in front of the tire shop bay

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Cracks and vegetation growth in the sidewalk create minor tripping hazards and indicate poor maintenance.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the curb cut to the minimum necessary for vehicle access to slow turning speeds and reduce the pedestrian conflict area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a landscaped buffer or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair cracks and remove weeds from the sidewalk to ensure a smooth, accessible walking surface.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a sidewalk on one side of a wide, likely one-way street, with no physical buffer from traffic. There are no marked crossings or traffic calming features visible, which may encourage higher vehicle speeds and increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible for pedestrians to cross the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Absence of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway, exposing pedestrians to traffic without a safety zone.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks to provide safe and visible crossing locations for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and slow traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by industrial land use and a significant lack of infrastructure on the near side of the roadway. While a paved walkway exists on the far side, it is separated from the travel lanes by a wide drainage swale and lacks any visible marked crossing points for access.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the near side of the road, forcing pedestrians to walk in the grass or the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible to allow safe passage across the two-lane road to the far-side walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Physical Barrier to Walkway
hazards.description: A wide, unpaved drainage swale separates the roadway from the far-side sidewalk, creating a tripping hazard and accessibility barrier.
hazards.location_in_image: Between the road and the far-side white paved area

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous paved sidewalk on the near side of the street to complete the pedestrian network.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with pedestrian warning signs to facilitate safe crossing between sides of the street.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lower-height lighting focused on the walkways to improve visibility and security for pedestrians at night.
